brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.requirement: Compact desk unit with a drawer
requirements.evidence: A drawer (drawer:0#0,-1#cut, south-half drawer) sits on the cut face of the north half-base at (0,-1). Build is 8 parts.

requirements.requirement: A spike at a corner where three bases meet, holding a small platform
requirements.evidence: Mount spike spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 sits at the junction where full bases (0,0), (0,1), (1,0) meet; check_build meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: The spike holds a small platform (platform accessory on the spike)
requirements.evidence: setSpikeAccessory platform-sm on the mount spike; BOM lists Platform, small x1. (Solid spike refused platforms, so spike was changed to mount type.)
8 parts total (4 pieces, 1 drawer, 1 spike, 2 joint bolts) - under 20.

finish.summary: Built a compact desk unit: four hex bases (three full bases meeting at a corner plus a north half-base), a south-half drawer on the half-base's cut face, and a mount-type spike at the three-base junction carrying a small platform. Two joint bolts lock the bases so check_build reports no loose-body warnings and meshClash is clear. Nothing was verified for load or material; the unit is printed PETG per the BOM notes.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
